bib.title: ROSCOE: A Suite of Metrics for Scoring Step-by-Step Reasoning

read.skipped: Appendix tables 18-39 (per-dataset, per-perturbation correlation grids) and Tables 12-13, 40-41 (example instances) were sampled for headers and captions, not read cell by cell.

question: How can the correctness of an LLM's step-by-step reasoning chain be scored automatically, without a gold reference chain and independent of the final answer?
hypothesis: Reference-free, interpretable metrics built on step-level alignment, embedding similarity, NLI contradiction and fluency will correlate better with reasoning errors than text-generation metrics such as ROUGE, BERTScore and BARTScore.
contributions: A taxonomy of reasoning errors, used for human annotation and synthetic datasets.
ROSCOE, a suite of 18 interpretable metrics (semantic alignment, semantic similarity, logical inference, language coherence) at step and chain level.
Comparative analysis on 11 datasets (6 diagnostic, 5 human judged) against baseline metrics.

method.summary: Metrics score a hypothesis chain h against source context s (reference-free) or reference chain r. Sentence embeddings (SimCSE finetuned with contrastive loss on perturbed gold chains) give cosine-based alignment and similarity scores; an NLI model gives contradiction probabilities; GPT2-Large perplexity and a grammar classifier give fluency. Metrics are meta-evaluated by Somers' D against synthetic perturbation labels and expert human error labels.

training.objective: SimCSE contrastive loss with in-batch negatives (cross-entropy); positive (s,r), hard negative (s,h) with h a perturbed reference; source and whole chain embedded as one text
training.steps: best checkpoint chosen by evaluating every 100 steps on dev
training.seeds: inference seed 42; without it embedding scores varied by about 0.01

other.samples_per_dataset: 500,000 sampled with replacement from each dataset
other.hparam_search: batch size {32,64,256,512,1024,2048}, lr {5e-06,1e-05,5e-05,1e-04}, max seq len {64,128,512}; not all combinations tried
other.validation: checkpoint maximising mean [cos(s_i,r_i) - cos(s_i,h_i)]/2 on perturbed dev chains

inference.samples: one score per chain; inference seed 42
inference.prompting: GPT-3 chains for human-judged sets: 2-shot or few-shot in-context examples, 'Explain if premise entails hypothesis.' style prompts (App. B, Table 9)

parameters.score_range: each ROSCOE metric bounded in [0,1], 1 best

metrics.name: Somers' D
metrics.definition: D(Y|X)=tau(X,Y)/tau(X,X) between metric score Y and perturbation or error indicator X; SciPy; p<0.05 required, non-significant omitted

eval.protocol: Diagnostics: 12 perturbation rules applied to half of gold chains, binary label per chain, max correlation across perturbations. Human judged: five expert annotators rate overall quality and coherence (Likert 1-5) and mark each of 9 error types per step (Y/N); max correlation across error types. Number of annotators per item and agreement not stated.

prompts.text:
I will explain how to make logical inferences:
Context: John wakes to the sound of his children giggling outside the door. They bust in and say "Happy Father's Day!" with a plate full of food. 2022 has been a great year.
Question: Can we infer that John was born before the inauguration of Barack Obama?
Explanation: We can infer that John is a father because of "his children". We can infer that the current year is 2022. Barack Obama was inaugurated in 2009, so it has been about 13 years since Obama was inaugurated. John's children are old enough to speak, so if John were born after Obama's inauguration, he would have been younger than 10 when he had children. So, we can infer that John was born before Obama's inauguration. The answer is "yes".
(second exemplar about Sam, a piano and Juilliard omitted here; see App. B)

results.claim: Expert annotation of at most 5 examples took an average 754 seconds (about 2.5 minutes per example); crowd workers paid over $30 an hour could not annotate accurately.
Embedding-based scores varied by about 0.01 across runs unless the seed was fixed at 42.

limits: Authors concede the taxonomy does not cover all reasoning errors and that use of the metrics to improve downstream task performance is left to future work (App A).
Human-judged sets are small (151-210 instances each) and mostly GPT-3 outputs; no inter-annotator agreement reported in the text read.
Reported correlation is the maximum over perturbation or error types per dataset, which favours metrics with many variants and overstates typical performance.
Moderate correlations with human judgement; metrics fail on missing-step errors and scores drift across datasets so fixed thresholds do not transfer.
ProofWriter results are low because correct proofs may order facts freely.
Ethics statement: metrics do not check integrity or bias of explanations.
Dated: baselines are 2020-2021 text-generation metrics; no LLM-as-judge baseline.

terms.definition: measures the ordinal association between two measured quantities; D(Y|X)=tau(X,Y)/tau(X,X), preferred over Kendall tau because it handles ties of a biased random variable better
r-align(h_i->s)=[1+max_j cos(h_i,s_j)]/2, normalized cosine similarity between a hypothesis step and the most similar context sentence
uses source and hypothesis (h->s); reference-based uses hypothesis and reference (h->r)
